meta.problem: Jeff and Shannon are working on their math homework, but Shannon feels Jeff is going ahead too fast without giving any help! So they decided to compare their homework to see if Jeff really was going ahead. Use the number lines to find out.

steps.answer: Yes; Jeff was going ahead with the homework.

hintsPerCorrectStep: What is the fraction that should be placed on this number line? Divide the number line by entering the number of divisions to make, and press OK.
The fraction 1/3 should be placed here. What is the denominator? Use the denominator to evenly divide the number line.
Enter 3 into the box and press OK.
Click on the spot where the first fraction would be on this number line.
What is the numerator of the fraction 1/3? The numerator represents the number of parts you should count.
Count 1 part(s) from the left and click on the spot.
What is the fraction that should be placed on this number line? Divide the number line by entering the number of divisions to make, and press OK.
The fraction 2/9 should be placed here. What is the denominator? Use the denominator to evenly divide the number line.
Enter 9 into the box and press OK.
Click on the spot where the second fraction would be on this number line.
What is the numerator of the fraction 2/9? The numerator represents the number of parts you should count.
Count 2 part(s) from the left and click on the spot.
Choose the correct statement from the choices. What are you looking for? The larger or smaller fraction?
You are looking for the fraction that is larger. Look at the fractions you placed on the number lines, which one is larger?
The larger fraction is placed on the number line for the Completion of Jeff's homework.
Click on the highlighted element and select 'Yes; Jeff was going ahead with the homework.'
You are done! Click on the "done" button to finish.
